subject: POC acceptance criteria, API route map, and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Arielle Chen <arielle@cartmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC acceptance criteria, API route map, and next steps

Hi Arielle — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a one-page scope that folds the items below into milestones (cartmetrics-poc-scope.xlsx).

Summary of what we heard from your team:
- Primary goal: Improve on-site product recommendations and reduce cart abandonment by surfacing better next-item predictions.
- Success signal: +6% add-to-cart rate in top 3 recommendation slots or a 10% lift in conversions for users in the cohort after 4 weeks.
- Data constraints: no PII sent, only hashed user ids and product ids; session context limited to last 10 events.

Proposed POC (3 weeks):
1) Week 1 — Integration & baseline: implement SDK client in staging, exercise text/structured calls, verify streaming token flow.
2) Week 2 — Tune & validate: run 1M inference queries (small sample), compare NDCG / add-to-cart to baseline.
3) Week 3 — Acceptance & handoff: finalize telemetry and roll plan for limited production gate.

Technical acceptance criteria (draft):
- API latency: median < 120ms for 1-2 token response paths (recommendation IDs).
- Throughput: sustain 250 rps in staging with 95th <= 300ms.
- Correctness: top-3 recommendations NDCG improvement >= 0.06 vs. baseline sample.
- Telemetry: per-route token counts, latency histograms, and a sample of 500 request/response pairs stored for debug.

Integration points and asks for your engineers:
- SDK: we will provide the JS + Python SDKs. Please expose one server-side route to proxy calls: POST /api/recommend with body { user_hash, session_events } and include X-Redwood-Client header.
- Streaming: optional — if you want incremental candidate scoring we can wire streaming over websocket / SSE; for first pass we suggest normal request/response.
- Tool calling: if you plan to surface enrichment (price/availability) from your catalog microservice, we can use Redwood function-calling to fetch the latest SKU metadata. That requires a single secure webhook endpoint reachable from our hosted runtime.

Next steps / owner list (proposed):
- CartMetrics: provide sample dataset and staging API credentials (ops@cartmetrics.com) — ACTION Arielle — by EOD Tue, Apr 3.
- Redwood: deliver SDK packages and API route spec — ACTION Ben — by Mon, Apr 1.
- Redwood engineering: assign engineer to streaming feasibility (if requested) — ACTION Marissa — by Mon, Apr 1.

Please confirm acceptance criteria and whether you want streaming in scope for week 1 or deferred to week 2. If you’d like, we can run a short kickoff next Tue/Thu.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: cartmetrics-poc-scope.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Arielle Chen <arielle@cartmetrics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@cartmetrics.com
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 18:35:22 -0700
Subject: Re: POC acceptance criteria, API route map, and next steps

Thanks Ben — appreciated the detailed recap. We’re aligned on the high-level goals; small edits below and a couple of questions.

Edits to success criteria:
- Keep the add-to-cart lift target but set a secondary metric: 5% reduction in cart abandonment for the test cohort after 30 days.
- For correctness, can we accept a slightly lower NDCG delta (>= 0.05) if the latency is <100ms? We’d prioritize latency in prod.

Questions:
1) Data sample: we can share a 30k-session anonymized sample (csv) by Tue. I’m attaching a suggested success-criteria CSV that maps our KPIs to the test cohorts.
2) Security: we need a quick note on how Redwood stores sample debug pairs (retention and redaction).
3) Streaming: we’re open to streaming but prefer to start without it — unless the SDK change would be minimal.

We’ll provide staging credentials to ops@redwood.inference (cc’d) — ACTION CartMetrics: ops@cartmetrics.com to send creds by Apr 3.

Looking forward to the kickoff — Tue morning works for me.

Thanks,
Arielle Chen
Head of Data Science
CartMetrics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

Cc: Arielle Chen <arielle@cartmetrics.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC acceptance criteria, API route map, and next steps

Looping in internal owners and mapping tasks to engineering — copied Arielle for visibility.

Internal split:
- Integration (edge + SDK): Stephanie will own the JS + Python SDK drops and the API contract (POST /api/recommend). ETA: Apr 1 for initial packages.
- Runtime perf & telemetry: I’ll take the baseline perf harness and the telemetry plumbing (token counts, histograms). ETA: Apr 5 will have the staging dashboards wired.
- Streaming / function-calling feasibility: Engineer assigned (Vik) will spike streaming websocket for incremental scoring; we’ll keep it out of week 1 unless Arielle requests otherwise.

API route mapping (draft):
- POST /api/recommend 
  - auth: Bearer token (rotating key).
  - body: { user_hash: string, session_events: [ { event_type, item_id, timestamp } ], k: int }
  - response: { recommendations: [ { item_id, score } ], model_version }
- POST /api/enrich (optional for function-calls)
  - acts as a server-side function-call from Redwood to CartMetrics to fetch price/availability; will use a one-time HMAC secret passed in setup.

Security note for Arielle:
- Debug pairs are stored in a locked S3 bucket accessible only to the engineering team; retention defaults to 30 days and PII is redacted at ingestion. We’ll provide a short SOC2-friendly summary before handshake.

Risks / blockers:
- Staging credentials and sample dataset (need by Apr 3).
- Agree on acceptance gating for NDCG vs latency tradeoff (Arielle’s note).
- If CartMetrics wants streaming in week 1 we’ll need to extend week 1 dev scope by 40% and push the demo to end of week 2.

Marissa
Director, Engineering
Redwood Inference
